export const meta = {
  name: 'adss-spikes',
  description: 'Four throwaway spikes answering what the interview could not: dlt raw landing, daana-cli on DuckDB, marimo as a destination, and the tooling gate',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Spike', detail: 'four independent probes, each in its own scratch directory, reporting findings only' },
  ],
}

const SCRATCH = '/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-adss-2026-09-07/45a0041f-5559-570b-bd39-1d1517807233/scratchpad/spikes'

const RULES = `
HARD RULES FOR THIS SPIKE
- You are a SPIKE. Your output is KNOWLEDGE, not code. Everything you write is thrown away.
- Work ONLY inside your own directory under ${SCRATCH}. Create it yourself.
- NEVER write, edit or create anything under /home/user/adss-2026-09-07. Never run git commands there.
- Do not install anything system-wide. Use \`uv\` for Python: \`uv init\`, \`uv add <pkg>\`, \`uv run <cmd>\` inside your own directory.
- Network works through a pre-configured proxy; plain https requests are fine.
- TIME-BOX: aim for roughly 20 focused tool calls. If something is not working by then, STOP and report exactly where it failed and what you saw. An honest "this does not work, here is the error" is a SUCCESSFUL spike. Do not grind.
- Report VERBATIM evidence: real command output, real file listings, real error text. Never describe what you expect; only what you observed. If you did not run it, say you did not run it.

CONTEXT
Someone is about to build a three-layer analytical platform in a fresh repo:
- DAS: dlt ingests a public OData API, lands parquet, unpacked into DuckDB as views. Schemas das__raw, das__staged.
- DAB: daana-cli (a Go binary) builds a focal/ensemble model. Schemas dab, dab__stage, dab__meta.
- DAR: a generated Puppini Unified Star Schema. Schema dar__uss.
- Destination: a marimo app reading dar__uss.
Everything lives in ONE DuckDB file. Python is managed with uv. Your findings decide the architecture, so precision matters more than success.

Already established (do not re-verify):
- daana-cli is at /home/user/adss-fable-poc/bin/linux-amd64/daana-cli and works.
- \`daana-cli install\` against a DuckDB connection profile works and creates schemas dab, dab__stage, dab__meta.
- A DuckDB connection profile looks like:
    connections:
      dev:
        type: duckdb
        database: ./warehouse.duckdb
        target_schema: dab
        stage_schema: dab__stage
        metadata_schema: dab__meta
- A full daana loop (install, deploy, execute) was proven against PostgreSQL and produced views view_<entity>, view_<entity>_hist, view_<entity>_with_rel, view_<src>_<rel>_<tgt>, and base tables <entity>_focal, <entity>_desc, <entity>_idfr, <src>_<tgt>_x.
- A working PostgreSQL example project (model.yaml, mappings/, workflow.yaml) is at
  /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-adss-2026-09-07/45a0041f-5559-570b-bd39-1d1517807233/scratchpad/cli-probe/quickstart-demo
  Copy from it rather than writing YAML from scratch. Read its files first.
`

const FINDING_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    spike: { type: 'string' },
    verdict: { type: 'string', enum: ['works', 'works-with-caveats', 'blocked', 'inconclusive'] },
    headline: { type: 'string', description: 'One sentence: the single most decision-relevant thing you learned' },
    findings: {
      type: 'array',
      description: 'Each an observed fact with the evidence that established it',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          claim: { type: 'string' },
          evidence: { type: 'string', description: 'Verbatim command and its real output, trimmed to what matters' },
          confidence: { type: 'string', enum: ['observed', 'inferred', 'assumed'] },
        },
        required: ['claim', 'evidence', 'confidence'],
      },
    },
    recipe: { type: 'string', description: 'The minimal working recipe you established, as commands and file contents someone could reproduce. Empty if blocked.' },
    gotchas: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'Things that will waste a day if not known up front' },
    openQuestions: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'What you could not settle in the time-box' },
    versions: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'Exact versions of everything you installed' },
  },
  required: ['spike', 'verdict', 'headline', 'findings', 'recipe', 'gotchas', 'openQuestions', 'versions'],
}

const SPIKES = [
  {
    key: 'dlt-raw-landing',
    prompt: `${RULES}

SPIKE 1 — dlt landing a whole payload as parquet, read back through DuckDB views.

The architecture requires FORGIVING INGESTION and STRICT UNPACKING: dlt must NOT infer a schema and normalise the source into typed columns. Each source record must land as ONE row holding the record as a single JSON value, plus provenance columns, written to parquet, append-only, never updated.

Answer these, in order:
1. Does \`uv add dlt\` work here, and what version lands? Does it need extras for parquet/filesystem/duckdb?
2. Can a dlt resource be made to land ONE column containing the whole record as JSON, with normalisation NOT splitting it into columns? Try the approaches that exist (yielding a dict whose single field is a json string; a column hint of type json/text; disabling/limiting normalisation via max_table_nesting or a column schema) and report which actually works.
3. Land at least 50 real records from https://demodata.grapecity.com/northwind/odata/v1/Orders (the rows are under the "value" key; \`$count=true\` and \`$top\`/\`$skip\` work) into parquet on the local filesystem via the filesystem destination.
4. What does the resulting directory and parquet file actually look like? Show the file layout and \`DESCRIBE\` of the parquet from DuckDB.
5. Which dlt-added metadata columns appear (_dlt_load_id, _dlt_id, others)? Are they enough to answer "which load, from where, when" for a single row, or must the pipeline add its own provenance columns? Recommend the exact provenance columns to add.
6. Confirm write_disposition="append" leaves earlier files intact across two runs. Run it TWICE and show both loads present.
7. From DuckDB (\`uv add duckdb\`), create a view over the parquet glob and then a second view that extracts and casts a few typed columns out of the JSON column. Show the SQL that works and the query results. Note the exact JSON functions DuckDB wants.

Report the minimal working recipe verbatim.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'daana-on-duckdb',
    prompt: `${RULES}

SPIKE 2 — daana-cli deploy + execute against DuckDB, reading VIEWS as mapping sources, and what historization it produces.

This is the highest-risk spike: the whole DAB layer depends on it.

Setup: make your own directory, put a DuckDB connections profile in it (shape given above), and copy model.yaml, mappings/ and workflow.yaml from the PostgreSQL example project named above. Then:

1. Create a DuckDB file yourself first (\`uv add duckdb\`), and inside it create a schema named das__staged containing the source data the mappings expect. IMPORTANT: create them as VIEWS, not tables — DAB must read a view. The PostgreSQL example's mappings read stage.customers, stage.customer_addresses, stage.loyalty_memberships and stage.sales_orders; the data SQL is at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-adss-2026-09-07/45a0041f-5559-570b-bd39-1d1517807233/scratchpad/cli-probe/quickstart-demo/data/ but it is PostgreSQL DDL, so it may be quicker to invent a handful of equivalent rows yourself with matching column names than to port it. Either is fine — say which you did.
2. Point the mappings at das__staged.<table> instead of stage.<table>, and set connection to your duckdb profile name.
3. Run \`daana-cli install\`, \`daana-cli check workflow\`, \`daana-cli deploy\`, \`daana-cli execute\` (all with --no-tui). Report the OUTCOME OF EACH, including any failure verbatim.
4. If it works: list every object daana created in dab, dab__stage and dab__meta, and show \`DESCRIBE\` plus a few rows of view_<entity>, view_<entity>_hist and the relationship view. Are the names and shapes IDENTICAL to the PostgreSQL run described above, or do they differ on DuckDB?
5. THE HISTORIZATION QUESTION. The real build will date every DAB version by WHEN DAS OBSERVED THE ROW — a load timestamp column on the staged view — using \`entity_effective_timestamp_expression: <that column>\`. Test this: give your staged views a load-timestamp column, map it as the effective timestamp, execute; then CHANGE one attribute value for one key AND give it a later load timestamp, execute again. Report exactly what view_<entity> and view_<entity>_hist contain afterwards. Does the history keep both versions? Does the current view show the new one?
6. Do this for BOTH \`ingestion_strategy: FULL\` and \`ingestion_strategy: FULL_LOG\` if the time-box allows — the difference between them on a re-load is a decision the build depends on. If you only have time for one, do FULL and say so.
7. Note anything DuckDB-specific: identifier casing and quoting, whether daana needs the file to not be open by another process, concurrency errors, whether execute is re-runnable.

This spike's findings matter more than its tidiness. Report failures in full.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'marimo-destination',
    prompt: `${RULES}

SPIKE 3 — marimo as the destination: reading DuckDB, exporting, and being screenshotted headless.

Each slice ends in a marimo app that presents a business question and its answer, read from a DuckDB warehouse. Acceptance happens by screenshots posted to a pull request, and the user also wants to run the app themselves.

1. Does \`uv add marimo\` work, and what version? What does it pull in?
2. Make a tiny DuckDB file with one table of a few rows (\`uv add duckdb\`). Write a marimo notebook that reads it and shows: a title, the question as prose, a table of the answer, and a chart. Which plotting library works most cleanly inside marimo without extra setup — altair, plotly, matplotlib? Report what you actually got working.
3. Can the notebook be run as an APP (\`marimo run\`) rather than an editable notebook, headless, on a fixed port with no browser opening? Show the exact command and that it serves.
4. EXPORT: what export formats does this version support (\`marimo export --help\`)? Get an actual export to static HTML working and report the resulting file SIZE. Does the export include the rendered chart and table output, or only the code? Try the flags that control that.
5. SCREENSHOTS — this is the acceptance mechanism, so establish it properly. Chromium is at /opt/pw-browsers/chromium with PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers and PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD=1 already set; do NOT run \`playwright install\`. Using \`uv add playwright\`, drive headless Chromium to open the running marimo app (or the exported HTML) and save a PNG. Confirm the PNG is a real rendering of the app — check its byte size and dimensions, and say how you know it is not blank. Report the exact script that worked.
6. Note the gotchas: does marimo need a writable config dir, does it complain without a TTY, does the app need a moment before the chart renders, does the export need the notebook to have been executed first?

The deliverable is a reproducible recipe for "build the app, run it, screenshot it, export it".`,
  },
  {
    key: 'tooling-gate',
    prompt: `${RULES}

SPIKE 4 — the quality gate, on the exact artefacts this repository will contain.

The repository will be gated by ruff, a strict type checker, sqlfluff over ALL SQL including generated SQL, yamllint, and pytest, run by pre-commit locally and in CI. Establish that each of these actually works on the shapes involved, and find where they fight.

1. \`uv init\` a project and \`uv add --dev ruff sqlfluff yamllint pytest pre-commit\` plus a type checker. For the type checker, try \`ty\` first (Astral's, likely fastest and newest); if it is not viable report why and fall back to mypy. Report versions of everything.
2. RUFF: confirm lint and format run. Nothing subtle expected — just confirm and report the version.
3. TYPE CHECKER — the important part. The build has a typed domain model of the machinery: frozen dataclasses with enums, tuples of nested dataclasses, and a discriminated union of stage kinds. Write a ~60-line module in that shape, plus one deliberate type error, and confirm the checker in STRICT mode flags the error and passes when fixed. Report the exact configuration needed and any friction with frozen dataclasses or unions.
4. SQLFLUFF — the highest-risk of these. The repository will generate DuckDB SQL. Determine: does this sqlfluff version have a \`duckdb\` dialect (\`uv run sqlfluff dialects\`)? If not, which dialect is the least-wrong stand-in? Then lint a piece of SQL in the style this build will emit — a UNION ALL of several SELECT branches, each branch aliasing every column of one fixed column list with AS, \`cast(x AS DECIMAL(28, 8))\`, lower-case function names, UPPER-case keywords, double-quoted mixed-case identifiers crossing over from the business layer, a \`QUALIFY row_number() OVER (...)\` clause, and a quoted reserved word used as a table name (\`"order"\`). Report EVERY rule that fires, and for each say whether the right fix is to change the SQL the generator emits or to configure the rule off — with the reason.
5. YAMLLINT: lint a YAML file in the shape of a data contract — nested block mappings, some short flow mappings like \`{source_path: OrderId, target_name: order_id, type: INTEGER}\`, lines up to ~150 chars. Report which default rules fire and the minimal sane configuration.
6. PRE-COMMIT: get a .pre-commit-config.yaml running all of the above locally with \`uv run pre-commit run --all-files\`. Report whether the hooks work offline / from local venv rather than fetching remote repos, since CI determinism matters.

The deliverable is: exact versions, exact config files, and the list of sqlfluff rules that will fight generated SQL.`,
  },
]

phase('Spike')

const results = (await parallel(SPIKES.map(s => () =>
  agent(s.prompt, { label: s.key, phase: 'Spike', schema: FINDING_SCHEMA })
))).filter(Boolean)

log(`${results.length}/${SPIKES.length} spikes reported`)

return results

result.spike: SPIKE 1 — dlt landing a whole OData payload as one JSON column per record into append-only parquet, read back through DuckDB views (DAS layer: forgiving ingestion / strict unpacking)
result.headline: A dlt resource with `columns={"payload": {"data_type": "json"}}` lands each source record as exactly one JSON column with zero child tables and zero column inference — but dlt silently renames the dataset `das__raw` to `das_raw` unless you pass `enable_dataset_name_normalization=False`, and DuckDB silently drops columns across an evolving parquet glob unless you pass `union_by_name => true`.

findings.claim: `uv add "dlt[filesystem,duckdb,parquet]" duckdb` works with no system-wide install and no .dlt config directory needed. dlt 1.30.0, duckdb 1.5.5, pyarrow 25.0.1.
findings.evidence:
$ uv add "dlt[filesystem,duckdb,parquet]" duckdb
 + fsspec==2026.7.0
 + pyarrow==25.0.1
 + s3fs==2026.7.0
 ...
$ uv run python -c "import dlt, duckdb, pyarrow; ..."
dlt 1.30.0
duckdb 1.5.5
pyarrow 25.0.1

$ ls -a   # after 5 successful pipeline runs
.  ..  .git  .gitignore  .python-version  .venv  README.md  _lake  _lake2  _lake3  ... pyproject.toml  uv.lock
$ ls -a .dlt
ls: cannot access '.dlt': No such file or directory

findings.claim: APPROACH B WINS: `@dlt.resource(columns={"payload": {"data_type": "json"}})` yielding a real dict under `payload` keeps the whole record in ONE column of dlt type `json`. No columns are inferred from inside it.
findings.evidence:
--- orders_b_jsonhint ---
  payload                  json
  _src_url                 text
  _extracted_at            timestamp
  _page_index              bigint
  _dlt_load_id             text
  _dlt_id                  text

findings.claim: Approach B survives NESTED objects and arrays with no child tables. A record containing {"Nested":{"a":1,"b":{"c":2}},"Arr":[{"x":1},{"x":2}]} produced no `probe_b_jsonhint__arr` table.
findings.evidence:
=== TABLES CREATED === ['_dlt_loads', '_dlt_pipeline_state', '_dlt_version', 'probe_a_jsonstr', 'probe_b_jsonhint', 'probe_c_nest0']
--- probe_b_jsonhint --- {'payload': 'json', '_src_entity': 'text', '_dlt_load_id': 'text', '_dlt_id': 'text'}

-- roundtrip from DuckDB:
SELECT payload ->> '$.Id' id, payload -> '$.Nested.b.c' deep, json_array_length(payload,'$.Arr') arrlen ...
│ 1  │ 2 │ 2 │ {"Id":1,"Nested":{"a":1,"b":{"c":2}},"Arr":[{"x":1},{"x":2}],"Only1":"present"} │
│ 2  │ 8 │ 0 │ {"Id":2,"Nested":{"a":9,"b":{"c":8}},"Arr":[],"NewFieldLater":true}             │

findings.claim: APPROACH A also works: pre-serialising with json.dumps() gives a `text` column that DuckDB's JSON operators read identically. It is physically indistinguishable from B in parquet.

APPROACH C FAILS the requirement: `max_table_nesting=0` does NOT stop normalisation. Top-level keys are still split into snake_cased typed columns; it only collapses NESTED values into json strings instead of child tables.
findings.evidence:
--- orders_c_nest0 ---
  order_id                 bigint
  customer_id              text
  employee_id              bigint
  order_date               text
  freight                  double
  ...
  ship_region              text     <-- appended LAST: absent from first records, added by schema evolution

--- probe_c_nest0 --- {'id': 'bigint', 'nested': 'json', 'arr': 'json', 'only1': 'text', '_dlt_load_id': 'text', '_dlt_id': 'text', 'new_field_later': 'bool'}

findings.claim: 120 real Northwind Orders records (2 pages x $top=60 with $skip) landed to local filesystem parquet. The API reports @odata.count=830 total.
findings.evidence:
$ curl ".../Orders?$count=true&$top=2"
{"@odata.context":"...#Orders","@odata.count":830,"value":[{"OrderId":10248,...}]}

-- after two pipeline runs:
│    _dlt_load_id    │              das_run_id              │ rows  │ last_page │
│ 1788808160.6964235 │ 1a386e46-4045-4c94-b7ba-678677b9bce0 │   120 │         1 │
│ 1788808163.0261497 │ 9e119db3-9ba2-4693-ba71-91d520d39d3b │   120 │         1 │

findings.claim: Default filesystem layout is <bucket_url>/<dataset>/<table>/<load_id>.<file_id>.parquet — one parquet file per table per load, plus an `init` marker and three _dlt_* bookkeeping folders.
findings.evidence:
$ find _lake3 -type f | sort
_lake3/das__raw/_dlt_loads/das_ingest__1788808160.6964235.jsonl
_lake3/das__raw/_dlt_loads/das_ingest__1788808163.0261497.jsonl
_lake3/das__raw/_dlt_pipeline_state/das_ingest__1788808160.6964235__8a8996b9....jsonl
_lake3/das__raw/_dlt_version/das_ingest__1788808161.9497797__8a8996b9....jsonl
_lake3/das__raw/init
_lake3/das__raw/orders/1788808160.6964235.ec3a294455.parquet
_lake3/das__raw/orders/1788808163.0261497.091ef72a25.parquet

findings.claim: DESCRIBE of the landed parquet from DuckDB: payload is VARCHAR, dlt `timestamp` becomes TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, `bigint` becomes BIGINT.
findings.evidence:
$ DESCRIBE SELECT * FROM read_parquet('.../orders_a_jsonstr/*.parquet')
│ payload          │ VARCHAR                  │
│ _src_system      │ VARCHAR                  │
│ _src_entity      │ VARCHAR                  │
│ _src_url         │ VARCHAR                  │
│ _extracted_at    │ TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE │
│ _page_index      │ BIGINT                   │
│ _src_total_count │ BIGINT                   │
│ _payload_hash    │ VARCHAR                  │
│ _dlt_load_id     │ VARCHAR                  │
│ _dlt_id          │ VARCHAR                  │

findings.claim: dlt adds EXACTLY TWO metadata columns to a root table: `_dlt_load_id` and `_dlt_id`. Nothing else. They are NOT sufficient for 'which load, from where, when'.
findings.evidence:
COLUMNS: {'payload': 'json', 'das_source_system': 'text', ..., '_dlt_load_id': 'text', '_dlt_id': 'text'}
TABLES: ['_dlt_loads', '_dlt_pipeline_state', '_dlt_version', 'orders']

findings.claim: `_dlt_load_id` is only a unix-timestamp-ish string; the load's completion time and schema name live in a SEPARATE `_dlt_loads/*.jsonl` file — written as JSONL even when loader_file_format='parquet'. It is joinable but requires read_json_auto.
findings.evidence:
$ cat _lake/das_raw/_dlt_loads/*.jsonl
{"load_id":"1788808038.4446907","schema_name":"das_raw","status":0,"inserted_at":"2026-09-07T19:07:20.149618+00:00","schema_version_hash":"3OHo10rOiRa8CBYFQqqjRWFXcZmSvrWoOxFEpo6LF7Y="}

-- join works:
SELECT s._dlt_load_id, l.inserted_at, count(*) FROM das__staged.orders s
JOIN read_json_auto('_lake3/das__raw/_dlt_loads/*.jsonl') l ON l.load_id = s._dlt_load_id GROUP BY 1,2;
│ 1788808160.6964235 │ 2026-09-07 19:09:21.957398 │   120 │
│ 1788808163.0261497 │ 2026-09-07 19:09:24.2284   │   120 │

findings.claim: `_dlt_id` is a per-row-instance surrogate, NOT a stable record identity. The same source record (OrderId 10248) got a different _dlt_id in each load. Content identity must come from your own hash column.
findings.evidence:
│ 10248 │ VINET │ ... │ 1788808038.4446907 │ b6aVmzfAxRVPDA │
│ 10248 │ VINET │ ... │ 1788808057.5555441 │ z8O+0F4oaJbS5A │

-- and the content hash IS stable:
│ all_rows │ distinct_orders │ loads │ distinct_payloads │
│      240 │             120 │     2 │               120 │

findings.claim: write_disposition='append' leaves earlier files intact. Two runs of the identical pipeline produced two parquet files per table and two rows in _dlt_loads; nothing was overwritten.

CRITICAL: dataset_name='das__raw' is silently normalised to 'das_raw' (double underscore collapsed). Passing enable_dataset_name_normalization=False on the destination preserves the literal 'das__raw' folder.
findings.evidence:
-- default:
|dlt|client.py|_normalize_identifier:364|Due to normalization dataset name got changed from 'das__raw' to 'das_raw which will be used to create db schemas or folders. ... We suggest that you use dataset names that do not need to be normalized or disable dataset name normalization via `enable_dataset_name_normalization` on destination configuration.
$ find _lake -type f | head -1
_lake/das_raw/_dlt_loads/das_raw__1788808038.4446907.jsonl

-- with enable_dataset_name_normalization=False:
1 load package(s) were loaded to destination filesystem and into dataset das__raw
$ find _lake2 -type f | sort
_lake2/das__raw/probe_a_jsonstr/1788808114.2206264.eab5790abd.parquet

findings.claim: CRITICAL: a plain read_parquet glob over an append-only lake SILENTLY DROPS columns added in later loads — no error, just missing data. `union_by_name => true` fixes it.
findings.evidence:
-- load 2 added _new_prov_col. Plain glob:
SELECT * FROM read_parquet('.../probe_a_jsonstr/*.parquet')
│ payload │ _src_entity │ _dlt_load_id │ _dlt_id │      <-- _new_prov_col ABSENT, 3 rows returned, no error

-- with union_by_name:
SELECT * FROM read_parquet('.../probe_a_jsonstr/*.parquet', union_by_name => true)
│ payload │ _src_entity │ _dlt_load_id │ _dlt_id │ _new_prov_col │
│ {"Id": 1, ...} │ Probe │ 1788808114.2206264 │ e6EAQCnsZXGpKA │ NULL │
│ {"Id": 3}      │ Probe │ 1788808135.4990737 │ zp4ZUCgyYhgUnw │ v2   │

findings.claim: DuckDB JSON operators work directly on the VARCHAR payload column with an implicit cast — no explicit ::JSON needed. `->>` yields VARCHAR (then CAST), `->` yields JSON, plus json_keys / json_array_length / json_extract.
findings.evidence:
CAST(payload ->> '$.OrderId' AS BIGINT) AS order_id
│ order_id │ customer_id │ employee_id │ order_date │ shipped_date │    freight    │ ship_country │
│  int64   │   varchar   │    int32    │    date    │     date     │ decimal(18,4) │   varchar    │
│    10248 │ VINET       │           5 │ 1996-07-04 │ 1996-07-16   │       32.3800 │ France       │

SELECT json_keys(payload) FROM ... LIMIT 1
[CustomerId, EmployeeId, Freight, OrderDate, OrderId, RequiredDate, ShipAddress, ShipCity, ShipCountry, ShipName, ShipPostalCode, ShipRegion, ShipVia, ShippedDate]

findings.claim: The strict layer recovers precision the forgiving layer would have lost: freight is DOUBLE when dlt infers it (approach C), but DECIMAL(18,4) when cast explicitly out of the JSON column. This is a concrete argument for the two-layer design.
findings.evidence:
-- inferred by dlt (approach C):
│ freight          │ DOUBLE      │
-- cast in das__staged:
│ freight          │ DECIMAL(18,4)            │

SELECT ship_country, count(*) n, round(sum(freight),2) freight ... 
│ Germany      │    20 │       1861.32 │
│ Brazil       │    18 │        541.98 │

findings.claim: Hive-style date partitioning works via the filesystem `layout` parameter, but the placeholder names are {YYYY}/{MM}/{DD}, not {year}/{month}/{day}.
findings.evidence:
-- with {year}-{month}-{day}:
dlt.destinations.exceptions.InvalidFilesystemLayout: ... expected placeholders: `{'H', 'm', 'HH', 'DD', 'dd', 'SSSS', 'D', 'load_id', 'ss', 'Y', 'file_id', 'S', 'schema_name', 'dddd', 'load_package_timestamp', 'ext', 'Q', 'd', 'ddd', 'timestamp_ms', 'MM', 'table_name', 'MMMM', 'load_package_timestamp_ms', 'mm', 'YY', 'YYYY', 'M', 'MMM', 'timestamp', 's', 'SS', 'curr_date', 'SSS'}` Missing placeholders: `['year', 'month', 'day']`

-- with {YYYY}-{MM}-{DD}:

## Ingestion — /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-adss-2026-09-07/45a0041f-5559-570b-bd39-1d1517807233/scratchpad/spikes/spike1-dlt/recipe.py

    """DAS forgiving ingestion: one JSON column per source record, append-only parquet."""
    import os, uuid, hashlib, json
    from datetime import datetime, timezone
    import requests, dlt

    BASE = "https://demodata.grapecity.com/northwind/odata/v1/Orders"
    LAKE = os.path.abspath("./_lake3")
    PAGE = 60

    @dlt.resource(
        name="orders",
        write_disposition="append",
        columns={"payload": {"data_type": "json"}},   # <-- the whole trick
    )
    def odata_orders(page_size: int = PAGE, max_pages: int = 2):
        run_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
        for page in range(max_pages):
            url = f"{BASE}?$count=true&$top={page_size}&$skip={page * page_size}"
            resp = requests.get(url, timeout=60)
            resp.raise_for_status()
            fetched_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
            body = resp.json()
            for i, rec in enumerate(body["value"]):
                canon = json.dumps(rec, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True)
                yield {
                    "payload":            rec,                      # stays ONE json column
                    "das_source_system":  "northwind_odata",
                    "das_source_entity":  "Orders",
                    "das_request_url":    url,
                    "das_http_status":    resp.status_code,
                    "das_extracted_at":   fetched_at,
                    "das_run_id":         run_id,
                    "das_page_number":    page,
                    "das_page_offset":    i,
                    "das_record_hash":    hashlib.sha256(canon.encode()).hexdigest(),
                    "das_source_count":   body.get("@odata.count"),
                }

    pipeline = dlt.pipeline(
        pipeline_name="das_ingest",
        destination=dlt.destinations.filesystem(
            bucket_url=LAKE,
            enable_dataset_name_normalization=False,   # keeps the literal 'das__raw'
            # optional: layout="{table_name}/load_date={YYYY}-{MM}-{DD}/{load_id}.{file_id}.{ext}",
        ),
        dataset_name="das__raw",
    )
    info = pipeline.run(odata_orders(), loader_file_format="parquet")

## Recommended provenance columns (dlt's two are NOT enough)

Keep `_dlt_load_id` + `_dlt_id`, and ADD, on every raw row:

| column | why |
|---|---|
| `das_source_system` | which upstream system ("northwind_odata") |
| `das_source_entity` | which endpoint/entity ("Orders") |
| `das_request_url`   | the exact URL incl. `$top`/`$skip` — answers "from where" per row |
| `das_http_status`   | proves the row came from a 200 |
| `das_extracted_at`  | wall-clock of the HTTP call — answers "when" WITHOUT joining `_dlt_loads` |
| `das_run_id`        | uuid4 per pipeline invocation — groups pages of one logical run |
| `das_page_number` / `das_page_offset` | position within the paginated fetch; makes a row reproducible |
| `das_record_hash`   | sha256 of canonical json — the ONLY stable record identity; use for dedup, since `_dlt_id` changes every load |
| `das_source_count`  | `@odata.count` at fetch time — lets you detect truncated pulls |

Do NOT rely on `_dlt_id` for identity and do NOT rely on `_dlt_load_id` alone for time — the timestamp lives in a separate JSONL file.

## DuckDB views — /tmp/claude-0/.../spike1-dlt/views.sql (use ABSOLUTE paths in production)

    CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS das__raw;
    CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS das__staged;

    -- LAYER 1: forgiving. one view per source entity over the append-only parquet glob.
    CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW das__raw.orders AS
    SELECT *, filename AS das_source_file
    FROM read_parquet(
           '_lake3/das__raw/orders/*.parquet',
           filename      => true,
           union_by_name => true   -- MANDATORY: without it DuckDB uses file #1's schema
                                   -- and silently drops columns added in later loads
         );

    -- LAYER 2: strict. explicit casts out of the JSON text column.
    CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW das__staged.orders AS
    SELECT
      CAST(payload ->> '$.OrderId'      AS BIGINT)         AS order_id,
            payload ->> '$.CustomerId'                     AS customer_id,
      CAST(payload ->> '$.EmployeeId'   AS INTEGER)        AS employee_id,
      TRY_CAST(payload ->> '$.OrderDate'   AS DATE)        AS order_date,
      TRY_CAST(payload ->> '$.ShippedDate' AS DATE)        AS shipped_date,
      CAST(payload ->> '$.Freight'      AS DECIMAL(18,4))  AS freight,
            payload ->> '$.ShipCountry'                    AS ship_country,
            payload ->> '$.ShipRegion'                     AS ship_region,
      json_keys(payload)                                   AS payload_keys,
      _dlt_load_id, _dlt_id,
      das_source_system, das_source_entity, das_request_url,
      das_extracted_at, das_run_id, das_page_number, das_page_offset,
      das_record_hash, das_source_count, das_source_file
    FROM das__raw.orders;

JSON functions DuckDB actually wants (all work on a plain VARCHAR column, implicit cast, no `::JSON` needed):
- `payload ->> '$.Field'`          -> VARCHAR (then wrap in CAST / TRY_CAST)
- `payload -> '$.a.b.c'`           -> JSON (nested navigation)
- `json_keys(payload)`             -> VARCHAR[]
- `json_array_length(payload,'$.Arr')` -> UINT64
- `json_extract(payload, '$.X')`   -> JSON

gotchas: dataset_name='das__raw' is SILENTLY renamed to 'das_raw' (dlt collapses the double underscore). Only a WARNING log line tells you. Fix: dlt.destinations.filesystem(bucket_url=..., enable_dataset_name_normalization=False). If DAS/DAB/DAR all use double-underscore schema names, every dlt destination in the project needs this flag.

DuckDB read_parquet over a glob defaults to the FIRST file's schema and silently drops columns present only in later files — no error, no warning, just missing data. In an append-only lake where you may add a provenance column, always pass union_by_name => true.

max_table_nesting=0 is NOT the answer to 'do not normalise'. It only stops child tables; top-level keys still become snake_cased typed columns. Only the payload+data_type='json' hint (or pre-serialising with json.dumps) gives one column.

dlt's `json` data_type is NOT a parquet JSON logical type. parquet_schema() shows BYTE_ARRAY / UTF8 / StringType() — byte-identical to a text column. Anything downstream reading the parquet sees a VARCHAR, so the strict layer must cast, always.

_dlt_id is regenerated per load. The same source record has a different _dlt_id in every run (10248 was b6aVmzfAxRVPDA then z8O+0F4oaJbS5A). Never use it as a business or record key — add your own content hash.

_dlt_loads, _dlt_pipeline_state and _dlt_version are written as .jsonl even when loader_file_format='parquet'. To get a load's completion timestamp you must read_json_auto() the JSONL, not read_parquet(). Better: put das_extracted_at on every row so das__staged never needs that join.

dlt inferred freight as DOUBLE when it normalised the record (approach C). Money silently becomes floating point. The strict layer casting to DECIMAL(18,4) out of the JSON string is the fix — another reason not to let dlt infer.

Schema evolution is real and late: ship_region only appeared as a column AFTER the first records that had it null, and it landed at the END of the column list. Column ORDER in the parquet is not stable across loads — never rely on positional access.

Filesystem `layout` placeholders are arrow-style tokens ({YYYY}, {MM}, {DD}, {load_id}, {file_id}, {ext}, {table_name}, {schema_name}, {curr_date}) — {year}/{month}/{day} raise InvalidFilesystemLayout. The exception text conveniently lists the full valid set.

Relative paths inside a DuckDB view's read_parquet() resolve against the DuckDB process's cwd at QUERY time, not at CREATE VIEW time. A view created from the pipeline directory will break when marimo opens the same warehouse.duckdb from elsewhere. Use absolute paths, or a DuckDB variable/macro for the lake root.

Two identical runs produce 240 rows for 120 distinct orders. Append-only is correct for DAS but das__staged as written duplicates rows — a dedup/latest-version step (QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY das_extracted_at DESC)) is needed before DAB consumes it.
openQuestions: Deduplication strategy between das__raw and das__staged was NOT designed or tested. Two runs gave 240 rows / 120 distinct orders. Does DAB want the full append history, or a latest-version view? This changes whether das__staged is a plain cast view or a QUALIFY/ROW_NUMBER view.

Whether enable_dataset_name_normalization=False also disables TABLE name normalisation was not tested — every table name I used was already snake_case. If a source entity is named 'OrderDetails' it may still normalise to 'order_details'; verify before relying on literal names.

Not tested: whether DuckDB views over the parquet glob can live inside the SAME warehouse.duckdb that daana-cli installs into, and whether daana-cli's `install`/`deploy` tolerates extra user-created schemas (das__raw, das__staged) in that file.

Not tested at scale: 120 rows only. Memory/throughput behaviour with the full 830 Orders (or a large entity) and the cost of DuckDB scanning hundreds of small per-load parquet files was not measured. Small-file accumulation is the obvious risk of one file per load per table.

Not tested: incremental extraction (dlt's `dlt.sources.incremental`) against OData — I paginated manually. Whether a cursor on OrderDate/ModifiedDate coexists cleanly with the opaque single-JSON-column design is unverified.
Not tested: reading the parquet lake through DuckDB from a remote/object-store bucket_url (httpfs/s3fs). Only local filesystem was exercised, even though s3fs 2026.7.0 was installed.
Not tested: what happens when the OData API returns a non-200 or a malformed page mid-pagination — whether the load package is marked failed and whether partial pages are left in the lake.

gotchas: THE BIG ONE — never use `ingestion_strategy: FULL` against a das__staged view that can hold more than one row per primary key. Each execute silently inserts one extra duplicate row into <entity>_desc (22 -> 23 -> 24 -> 25 across three runs in my test), forever, and NONE of the presentation views show it: view_CUSTOMER stayed at 3 rows and view_CUSTOMER_hist at 4 rows the whole time. Since the DAS design is dlt landing parquet, an append/merge write disposition makes das__staged append-style by construction. Use FULL_LOG as the default; reserve FULL for views you can prove are exactly one row per key (dlt `replace` disposition). Switching back to FULL_LOG stops the bleeding but does NOT clean up rows already leaked — you must truncate <entity>_desc and re-execute.

ANY other open connection to the .duckdb file makes `daana-cli execute` fail, INCLUDING a read-only one, and the error message is a lie: 'daana framework is not installed on the remote database. Run daana-cli install first...'. The real DuckDB lock error is swallowed and does not appear even at --log-level debug. In this architecture the marimo app reading dar__uss, a dlt pipeline, or a stray `duckdb` REPL will all trigger it. The build needs an explicit single-writer discipline (a lock file, or a supervisor that stops readers before running the DAB step), and whoever operates it must be told that this error means 'the file is busy', not 'run install'.

Object names on DuckDB PRESERVE the model.yaml entity-id casing: view_CUSTOMER, CUSTOMER_focal, ORDER_CUSTOMER_x — not the lowercase view_customer PostgreSQL produced. Any DAR/USS generator that hardcodes lowercase names from the PG run will still work (DuckDB resolves case-insensitively, verified all four of view_customer / VIEW_CUSTOMER / "view_CUSTOMER" / "view_customer"), but code that string-matches names out of information_schema WILL break. Either lowercase model.yaml entity ids, or normalize when reading the catalog.

<entity>_focal and <entity>_idfr are created but stay EMPTY on DuckDB (0 rows for both CUSTOMER and ORDER) even though execute reports the 'execute_idfr_pipelines' phase as succeeding. All data is in <entity>_desc + <src>_<tgt>_x. If the DAR/USS generator was designed against the PostgreSQL run and joins to _focal or _idfr, it will produce empty results on DuckDB. Build DAR on the view_* layer only.

The presentation views are `SELECT * FROM dab.f_CUSTOMER()` — DuckDB TABLE MACROS. Macros do NOT appear in information_schema.tables or information_schema.routines-style catalog queries you might write by habit; you need duckdb_functions(). Any 'is DAB deployed?' health check that only looks at information_schema.tables will see the views but miss the macros they depend on.

view_<entity>_with_rel carries NO relationship key columns — its column list is byte-identical to view_<entity>. The name suggests it denormalizes the foreign keys; it does not. Get relationship keys from view_<src>_<rel>_<tgt> (ORDER_key, CUSTOMER_key, type_key, eff_tmstp, ver_tmstp).

Every numeric attribute comes back as DECIMAL(28,8) regardless of source type (my DECIMAL(12,2) became 220.25000000). marimo/plotting code downstream should format explicitly rather than trusting the source scale.
`daana-cli version` is not a command (Error: unknown command "version"). The version flag is `-v` / `--version`. Trivial, but it will waste a minute in CI.

The daana-cli --help text lists 'Multi-database support (PostgreSQL, BigQuery, Snowflake, Oracle, SQL Server)' — DuckDB is NOT advertised. It works fully, but this is unadvertised/possibly-untested territory, which is consistent with the FULL duplication bug and the empty _focal/_idfr tables. Do not expect DuckDB parity to be maintained by the vendor.

deploy is re-runnable after editing a mapping (I changed ingestion_strategy and re-deployed four times, always exit 0). execute is re-runnable and idempotent under FULL_LOG and under TRANSACTIONAL, and only non-idempotent under FULL-on-multi-row-source.

If PG populates them, this is a DuckDB-specific defect worth reporting to the vendor and worth guarding in the DAR generator; if PG is also empty, they are simply vestigial and DAR should ignore them.

result.recipe:
## Reproducible recipe: build the app, run it, screenshot it, export it

### 0. Project setup (one time)

    mkdir -p dar-app && cd dar-app
    uv init --python 3.12 .
    uv add marimo duckdb polars pyarrow altair playwright
    # pyarrow is REQUIRED for duckdb .pl()/.arrow(); marimo does not pull it in.
    # matplotlib / plotly optional — both work, altair is the best fit.

Resulting pyproject.toml dependencies (verbatim, as produced):

    dependencies = [
        "altair>=6.2.2",
        "duckdb>=1.5.5",
        "marimo>=0.24.0",
        "matplotlib>=3.11.1",
        "playwright>=1.62.0",
        "plotly>=7.0.0",
        "polars>=1.44.1",
        "pyarrow>=25.0.1",
    ]

### 1. Chromium shim (one time, no `playwright install`, nothing system-wide)

Playwright 1.62.0 wants chromium build **1234**; the image ships **1194**. Create a
symlink tree and point PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH at it:

    PW="$PWD/.pw-browsers"
    mkdir -p "$PW/chromium_headless_shell-1234/chrome-headless-shell-linux64" "$PW/chromium-1234"
    ln -sfn /opt/pw-browsers/chromium_headless_shell-1194/chrome-linux/headless_shell \
            "$PW/chromium_headless_shell-1234/chrome-headless-shell-linux64/chrome-headless-shell"
    ln -sfn /opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux "$PW/chromium-1234/chrome-linux"
    export PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="$PW"

(If the real build number differs after a playwright bump, read it off the error message
— it names the exact path it looked for.)

### 2. The notebook — dar_app.py

A marimo notebook is a plain .py of `@app.cell` functions; cell order in the file does
not matter, marimo resolves the DAG from the return values.

    import marimo
    __generated_with = "0.24.0"
    app = marimo.App(width="medium")

    @app.cell
    def _():
        import marimo as mo, duckdb, pathlib
        import altair as alt
        return alt, duckdb, mo, pathlib

    @app.cell
    def _(mo):
        mo.md(r"""
        # DAR — Regional revenue
        ## Business question
        **Which region generated the most revenue in H1, and how did it move
        month over month?**
        Answered directly from `dar__uss.stg_sales` in the shared DuckDB warehouse.
        """)
        return

    @app.cell
    def _(duckdb, pathlib):
        # __file__ works inside a marimo cell — anchor the DB relative to the notebook,
        # NOT to the cwd, or `marimo export`/`thumbnail` from another dir will break.
        DB = pathlib.Path(__file__).parent / "warehouse.duckdb"
        con = duckdb.connect(str(DB), read_only=True)   # read_only lets the app coexist
        return (con,)                                    # with a writer on the same file

    @app.cell
    def _(con):
        answer = con.execute("""
            SELECT region,
                   CAST(SUM(revenue) AS DOUBLE) AS revenue,   -- CAST: altair cannot
                   SUM(orders)                  AS orders     -- encode DuckDB DECIMAL
            FROM dar__uss.stg_sales GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY revenue DESC
        """).pl()
        answer            # bare name on the last line == the cell's rendered output
        return (answer,)  # -> marimo's interactive table widget

    @app.cell
    def _(answer, mo):
        top = answer.row(0, named=True)
        mo.md(f"### Answer\n\n**{top['region']}** leads with **{top['revenue']:,.2f}** "
              f"across **{top['orders']}** orders.")
        return

    @app.cell
    def _(alt, answer, mo):
        bar = (alt.Chart(answer).mark_bar()
                 .encode(x=alt.X("region:N", sort="-y", title="Region"),
                         y=alt.Y("revenue:Q", title="Revenue"),
                         color=alt.Color("region:N", legend=None))
                 .properties(width=420, height=240, title="Revenue by region"))
        chart = mo.ui.altair_chart(bar)   # mo.ui.altair_chart adds selection/interaction
        chart
        return

    if __name__ == "__main__":
        app.run()

Lint it before committing:  `uv run marimo check dar_app.py`

### 3. Run it as an app (what the user runs themselves)

    uv run marimo run dar_app.py --headless --host 127.0.0.1 --port 2718 --no-token

Comes up in ~1s, serves local assets, works with no internet.
Add `--include-code` only if you want viewers to see the source.
Readiness gate for CI:

    for i in $(seq 1 30); do sleep 1; \
      curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:2718/ | grep -q 200 && break; done

### 4. Screenshot — PREFERRED: no server needed

    PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="$PW" uv run marimo export thumbnail dar_app.py \
        --execute --width 1440 --height 1100 --scale 2 --timeout-ms 4000 \
        --output acceptance.png --overwrite
    # -> "Rendering dar_app.py... / Screenshotting -> acceptance.png... / ok"
    # -> 178026 bytes, 2880x2200 px, full render with charts.
    # --execute is MANDATORY (default is --no-execute = structure only, no outputs).

### 4b. Screenshot — alternative: drive the running app yourself
(more control: you can wait on specific selectors, capture console errors, crop)

    # shot.py
    import sys
    from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
    url, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    H = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 3400
    with sync_playwright() as p:
        b = p.chromium.launch(
            executable_path="/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome",
            args=["--no-sandbox", "--disable-dev-shm-usage"],
        )
        pg = b.new_page(viewport={"width": 1440, "height": H}, device_scale_factor=2)
        errs = []
        pg.on("pageerror", lambda e: errs.append(str(e)))
        pg.on("requestfailed", lambda r: errs.append(f"reqfail {r.url[:90]} {r.failure}"))
        pg.goto(url, wait_until="load", timeout=60_000)
        pg.wait_for_selector("text=Regional revenue", timeout=45_000)   # cell output
        pg.wait_for_selector(".vega-embed, .js-plotly-plot, canvas, img", timeout=45_000)
        pg.wait_for_timeout(3000)                                       # let vega paint
        pg.screenshot(path=out, full_page=True)
        assert not errs, errs
        b.close()

    uv run python shot.py http://127.0.0.1:2718/ acceptance.png 3400

Use `executable_path=` OR the step-1 shim; either alone is enough.

### 5. Prove the PNG is not blank (put this in CI so a white page fails the build)

    uv run python - <<'EOF'
    from PIL import Image; import sys
    im = Image.open("acceptance.png").convert("RGB")
    c = im.getcolors(maxcolors=10_000_000)
    assert len(c) > 500, f"looks blank: only {len(c)} distinct colours"
    print("dims", im.size, "distinct colours", len(c))
    EOF
    # good render:  dims (2880, 2200) distinct colours 3251..6198
    # blank render: distinct colours 1  (100% #ffffff)

### 6. Export to static HTML

    uv run marimo export html dar_app.py -o dar_app.html -f
    # 111,079 bytes for an 8-cell notebook. Runs the notebook itself — no prior
    # execution needed. Exit code is non-zero and cells are listed if any cell raises.
    # Add --no-include-code to strip source (byte-size was identical here; content differs).

**Do NOT use this file for acceptance screenshots.** It fetches every asset from
cdn.jsdelivr.net and is blank offline. Either screenshot the running server / use
`export thumbnail`, or make it self-contained yourself (UNTESTED):

    cp -r .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/marimo/_static/assets ./assets
    sed -i 's#https://cdn\.jsdelivr\.net/npm/@marimo-team/frontend@0\.24\.0/dist/#./#g' dar_app.html

### 7. Gitignore

    __marimo__/          # session cache written next to the notebook by `export html`
    .pw-browsers/        # the chromium symlink shim
gotchas: `marimo export html` output is NOT self-contained — it rewrites every JS/CSS/font to https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@marimo-team/frontend@<version>/dist/. Rendered without internet it is a 100%-white blank page (I measured exactly 1 distinct colour). Never screenshot the exported HTML for PR acceptance; screenshot the running server or use `marimo export thumbnail --execute`. There is no `--asset-url` CLI flag on `export html` — the override exists only in marimo's Python API (marimo/_templates.py, `asset_url`).

pyarrow is a hidden hard requirement. `uv add marimo duckdb` gives you neither pyarrow nor pandas, and `duckdb.execute(...).pl()` then dies with `No module named 'pyarrow'` in every dependent cell. Add pyarrow explicitly.

Playwright 1.62.0 looks for chromium build 1234; /opt/pw-browsers only has 1194. This breaks raw playwright AND marimo's own `export thumbnail` (which has no --executable-path flag). Fix with a symlink tree at a private PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH — do not run `playwright install`.
`marimo export thumbnail` defaults to --no-execute, which renders notebook STRUCTURE ONLY and produces a thumbnail with no outputs. You must pass --execute.

Playwright's full_page=True returns exactly the viewport height on a marimo app, not the document height — a 1000px viewport silently truncated the screenshot and lost two charts below the fold. Set a tall viewport (e.g. 1440x3400) rather than relying on full_page.

Charts need a settle delay. `wait_until="networkidle"` is not enough: marimo streams cell outputs over a WebSocket after page load, and vega/plotly paint after that. Wait on a text selector from an actual cell output, then on `.vega-embed/.js-plotly-plot/img`, then an extra ~3s. marimo's own thumbnail exporter has `--timeout-ms` (default 1500) for exactly this — bump it.
DuckDB DECIMAL columns arrive as polars `decimal[38,0]` and altair cannot encode them. CAST aggregates to DOUBLE in the SQL (this is a DAR-view design decision, not a notebook workaround).
Anchor the DuckDB path on `pathlib.Path(__file__).parent`, not the cwd. `marimo export` / `export thumbnail` are often invoked from elsewhere and a relative path breaks silently.
Open the warehouse with `duckdb.connect(path, read_only=True)`. DuckDB single-writer locking means a marimo app holding a read-write handle will block dlt or daana-cli from writing to the same file.

marimo auto-creates /root/.config/marimo/marimo.toml (0 bytes) on first invocation — the XDG config dir must be writable. It made no complaint at all about the absence of a TTY (stdin and stdout both non-tty throughout this spike).
`marimo export html` drops a `__marimo__/session/<notebook>.py.json` cache directory next to the notebook. Gitignore it.

Export failure is visible but soft: cells that raise are printed as `MarimoExceptionRaisedError: ...` and the command ends with `Error: Export was successful, but some cells failed to execute.` — the HTML is still written. Check the exit code in CI; do not assume a produced file means a good file.
openQuestions: Whether the sed-the-CDN-prefix + copy `marimo/_static/assets` trick actually produces a working self-contained HTML — I identified the mechanism (marimo/_templates.py line 521 does the reverse rewrite) but DID NOT run it or screenshot the result.
Whether `marimo export html-wasm` produces something self-contained enough to attach to a PR — not run at all.
Whether `marimo export pdf` works here (it likely needs a headless browser too and would hit the same 1194/1234 mismatch) — not run.
Which exact playwright version pairs with chromium build 1194, if you would rather pin than symlink — I did not look it up; the symlink shim made it moot.

Whether the served app renders correctly for a REMOTE viewer (the user running it themselves and hitting it over a tunnel) — I only tested 127.0.0.1. `--host`, `--base-url`, `--proxy` and `--allow-origins` all exist but were not exercised.
How marimo behaves when a dlt/daana writer holds the DuckDB write lock while the app is open, and whether `--watch` plus a re-run picks up new data. Not tested.
Whether `mo.ui.altair_chart` selections work in `marimo run` app mode (read-only) or only in edit mode — the widget rendered, but I never clicked it.
Whether `--no-include-code` genuinely removes the source: the two exports were byte-identical in SIZE (111079) yet differ at char 45218. I did not decode the payload to check what actually changed.

gotchas: SQLFLUFF RULE VERDICTS — the deliverable. AL09 (aliasing.self_alias.column): CONFIGURE OFF. It fires on `o.order_id AS order_id`, which is precisely the 'alias every column of one fixed column list with AS' discipline that makes UNION ALL branches positionally safe. Removing the alias to satisfy AL09 would delete the invariant. Non-negotiable exclude.

RF06 (references.quoting) 'Unnecessary quoted identifier': CONFIGURE OFF. Fires on every mixed-case identifier crossing from the business layer ("OrderPurchaseTs", "Stereotype") — six hits in a six-column view. It correctly leaves `dab."order"` alone. Note the subtlety: DuckDB is case-PRESERVING for unquoted identifiers (unlike Postgres, which folds to lower), so RF06's advice is technically safe in DuckDB — but a generator that quotes every business-layer name would need a case-sensitivity oracle to selectively unquote. Exclude and keep the generator dumb. Do NOT flip `prefer_quoted_identifiers = true` as the fix — that inverts the rule and then flags every unquoted snake_case column instead.

LT05 (layout.long_lines, default max 80) and LT09 (layout.select_targets): CONFIGURE OFF (or raise LT05 hard). A generator that emits one SELECT per line hits LT05 at 391 chars. Even a pretty-printing generator will blow 80 on `cast(x AS DECIMAL(28, 8)) AS long_business_column_name`. Set max_line_length = 120 AND exclude LT05, because generated SQL is not read by humans line-by-line. LT09 forces one select target per line — a formatting opinion the generator should not have to implement.

CV11 (convention.casting_style): FIX THE GENERATOR. Default policy is `consistent`, so mixing `cast()` and `::` in one file fails. Set `preferred_type_casting_style = cast` and make the generator emit `cast()` exclusively. `sqlfluff fix` auto-repairs this, so it is cheap either way.

RF02 (references.qualification) 'Unqualified reference in select with more than one referenced table': FIX THE GENERATOR — and it is the one rule sqlfluff CANNOT auto-fix ('2 unfixable linting violations found'). Any join-producing generator (view_<entity>_with_rel, view_<src>_<rel>_<tgt>) must table-qualify every column reference. This is a real correctness rule, not a style rule — keep it on.

LT14 (layout.keyword_newline): FIX THE GENERATOR, but for free — `sqlfluff fix` repairs it automatically. Just run `sqlfluff fix` as a generation post-step rather than teaching the generator about newlines.

yamllint walks into .venv/ by default and floods on third-party YAML (chardet ships a 2900-line training_metadata.yaml). `ignore: .venv/` in .yamllint.yaml is mandatory, or use `ignore-from-file: .gitignore`.

yamllint default line-length is 80 and the brief specifies ~150-char contract lines. `allow-non-breakable-inline-mappings: true` is what makes the short flow mappings `{source_path: ..., target_name: ..., type: INTEGER}` survive when they overrun — set it alongside max: 160.

ty is 0.0.78 — pre-1.0, pre-release version numbering. It works and is fast, but pin it exactly in uv.lock and expect diagnostic names/severities to churn. There is no `strict = true`; strictness is `--error all` on the CLI. If ty churn becomes intolerable the fallback is mypy --strict, but nothing observed here argues for it.

ty --error all does NOT flag fully unannotated functions. If you rely on ty alone for 'strict', untyped defs slip through. Ruff's ANN ruleset (ANN001/ANN201) is what closes that gap — keep ANN in the ruff select list or the type gate has a hole.

pre-commit's `ruff format` hook fails the run when it reformats a file ('files were modified by this hook'). That is expected pre-commit behaviour, but in CI it means the format hook is effectively a `--check`. Either accept the re-run, or use `ruff format --check` in the CI-only config.
openQuestions: Not tested: sqlfluff with `templater = jinja` or `dbt`. I set `templater = raw` because the generator emits literal SQL. If any SQL in the repo carries Jinja (dlt or a dar__uss template), the raw templater will produce PRS errors on `{{ }}` and the config needs a per-path override.

Not tested: DuckDB-specific syntax beyond QUALIFY — e.g. `SELECT * EXCLUDE (...)`, `SELECT * REPLACE (...)`, list/struct literals, `FROM tbl SELECT ...` (FROM-first), or `PIVOT`. The duckdb dialect inherits from postgres and may not cover all of these; worth a 5-minute probe before committing to sqlfluff over generated DDL.

Not tested: whether marimo notebook .py files survive ruff format and ty. marimo cells are decorated functions in a generated file; `@app.cell` functions typically lack return annotations and would trip ANN201, and marimo rewrites the file on save which fights ruff format. This needs its own probe — likely a per-path ruff `per-file-ignores` for the notebook directory.
Not tested: pytest against a real DuckDB file (no duckdb package was installed). Only a pure-python unit test ran.

Not measured: wall-clock cost of `sqlfluff lint` over a large generated-SQL tree. sqlfluff is the slowest of these by a wide margin; if the DAR generator emits hundreds of views, the pre-commit hook may need `--processes` or to be CI-only.

Not tested: a CI runner invoking these without a HOME writable for pre-commit's cache. I had to set HOME=$PWD/.pchome to run pre-commit in this sandbox; on a normal runner HOME exists, but the `repo: local` design means the cache holds almost nothing anyway.
